title: Turn the Fewest One-Way Streets Around

concept.title: Allow every street in both directions, but charge 1 for going against its arrow
body: A city has one-way streets (directed edges). You want to drive from node 1 to node `n`, and you may **turn some streets around** (reverse them). What is the fewest number of streets you must reverse so that a route from 1 to `n` exists?

Model this as a shortest-path problem with two kinds of moves for every street `u -> v`: going from `u` to `v` along the arrow costs **0** (nothing to reverse), and going from `v` to `u` against the arrow costs **1** (this street has to be reversed). The cheapest way from 1 to `n` in this graph is the answer, because a street that is used in a route is used in one direction only (a shortest route never uses a street twice).
All costs are 0 or 1, so the *0-1 BFS* with a double-ended queue is the right tool: a move of cost 0 puts the node at the **front** of the deque and a move of cost 1 at the **back**.
The time is O(n + m). If the answer is not finite, there is no route even when the directions are ignored: print -1.

statement: A directed graph has `n` nodes and `m` one-way streets. You may reverse the direction of some streets. Print the smallest number of streets you must reverse so that there is a route from node 1 to node `n`, or -1 if there is no route even if all streets could be used in both directions.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge that goes from the node `u` to the node `v`.
outputFormat: Print the number of streets or -1.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: The route 1, 2, 3, 4 uses the street 3 -> 2 against its direction: 1 street to reverse.

hints: For every street u -> v add an edge u to v with cost 0 and an edge v to u with cost 1.
Run a 0-1 BFS from node 1 using a deque.
Print the distance of node n, or -1 if it was not reached.

explanation: Every street gets a cost-0 edge along its direction and a cost-1 edge against it; a 0-1 BFS with a deque from node 1 gives the smallest number of reversals to reach node n.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

from collections import deque
INF = 10 ** 9
adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for u, v in edges:
    adj[u].append((v, 0))
    adj[v].append((u, 1))
dist = [INF] * (n + 1)
dist[1] = 0
dq = deque([1])
while dq:
    u = dq.popleft()
    for v, cost in adj[u]:
        if dist[u] + cost < dist[v]:
            dist[v] = dist[u] + cost
            if cost == 0:
                dq.appendleft(v)
            else:
                dq.append(v)
print(dist[n] if dist[n] < INF else -1)
